title: Additional Study for High-Risk Groups in the Child and Youth Welfare System Within the Main Study 'Res@t: Resource-Enhancing Training for Adolescents with Media-Related Disorders and Their Parents'
summary: The growing availability and attractiveness of digital media in recent decades has led to an increased need for care when it comes to the pathological use of digital media. Children and young people who come into contact with digital media at a young age are a particularly vulnerable group. The app-based support programme "Resource-Strengthening Training for Adolescents with Problematic Digital-Media Use and their Parents" ("Res@t" for short) is to be tested as a new form of care for its suitability for the treatment of media-related disorders (media dependency). An app is used to convey clinically established and scientifically proven programme content. The target group are adolescents (aged 10 to 19) who meet the clinical criteria for a Gaming Disorder according to ICD-11 or related media-related disorders in connection with the use of social media and streaming services, as well as their legal guardians, if possible. Unlike the project partners, this study focuses on an interlinked treatment approach (called "blended treatment") consisting of app intervention and outreach support in direct contact with high-risk groups that are difficult to reach (families receiving child and youth services, e.g. due to learning disabilities or prolonged absence from school).

interventions.name: The intervention group receives the app-based resource-strengthening adolescent and parent training programme (Res@t). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- receipt of child or youth welfare
- cut-off for disordered or hazardous media use in GADIS-A/-P, SOMEDIS-A/-P, or  STREDIS-A/P is reached
- fulfilled criteria for pathological or hazardous media use according to ICD-11 criteria (6C51, GC5Y, QE22, QE2Y)
Exclusion criteria:
- acute severe psychiatric disorders with a symptom burden that prevents participation in the study (i. e. psychotic disorders or disorders due to substance use)
- pervasive developmental disorders (i. e. autism spectrum disorder)
- acute suicidality
- inability to understand the study instructions (i. e. severe disorders of speech or language, intelligence or lack of german language skills)
